cases.title: First lesson, layers kind, on Mentor Practice 2: Dot 2's properties first (the tie), the Dots offered in one sentence, the learner picks them

rubric.reason: Turn 1 names the group with real members and the shared time ('Dot 2's Position, Opacity and Blurriness all run from 0.5 s to 1.5 s'), offers the other kind in one sentence ('Dot 1, Dot 2 and Dot 3 also all start at 0.5 s'), and lets the learner choose; the follow-up 'They start on the same frame and finish on the same frame' only restates the same group and never calls it everything that moves.

Both turns ask 'which should go first, and how far apart do you want them' as the learner's call, and the mentor never picks an order or gap; the learner hasn't answered yet, so there was nothing to repeat back.

Every name and time is backed: Dot 1/2/3, Position, Opacity, Blurriness, 0.5 s, 1.5 s and Seal (precomp) come from offset_snapshot, 1 s matches the preview_frame call and frame_together, and Title, Mentor Practice and 'about two weeks ago' come from the learner record (2026-10-12).

MENTOR: Last time, about two weeks ago, you eased Title's moves in Mentor Practice. This time we're in **Mentor Practice 2**, and we're working on timing: motion looks designed when things don't all move together.

If you'd rather work with whole layers, Dot 1, Dot 2 and Dot 3 also all start at 0.5 s, so you could stagger those instead.

I'm leaving Seal out because it's a precomp, and I can't check the timing inside it yet.

I tried to grab a frame at 1 s, but the image came back too small to show anything. Move the playhead to 1 s yourself and look at Dot 2. Its slide, its fade and its blur are all mid-move at that moment. When everything changes at once, nothing leads the eye, and the move reads as one flat event instead of something designed.

Do you want to stay with Dot 2's three properties, or switch to the three dots? Once you've picked, tell me **which should go first, and how far apart you want them.**
